title: The Salt of Money Is Chesed
summary: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakai rides out of Yerushalayim and meets the daughter of Nakdimon ben Gurion, once among the richest men in the city, gathering barley from the dung of Arab cattle. "The salt of money is chesed," she tells him, and her family's money was lost for lack of it. Then how much to give a poor person: "enough for his needs," Hillel running three mil before a poor man of a fine family, and the man who asked Rava for fat chicken and old wine, just as Rava's sister arrived with both.
key_ideas: The salt that preserves money is chesed: giving some away is what keeps it.
Give tzedakah properly and to the right places; how it is given matters.
Give a poor person what he is missing, even what he was used to before.
Hashem gives each person his food in its time, through whatever way He chooses.
